description:
Found while writing examples/codecs.exs (defk-9p6.19): in a hex encoder, `out = alloc(u8, 2 * len(a))` and then, for `i <- 0..(len(a) - 1)//1`, `out[2 * i] = @hex[band(bsr(b, 4), 15)]` and `out[2 * i + 1] = ...`, the generated C keeps the bounds check on `out[2 * i]` and `out[2 * i + 1]`, the overflow check on `2 * i`, and the u8 range check on a value that was read from a `[u8]` (so already 0..255). Three separate fact gaps:
1. Multiplication facts: `k * i` with a literal k >= 0 and i carrying `lb`/`ub` facts against an array length should get `ub: {arr => k*d}` only when scaled lengths are comparable: the length of `out` is `2 * len(a)`, so `in_bounds?` needs facts of the form "len(out) = k * len(a) + c" (alloc records its length expression's facts: today it keeps `len_lo`/`len_lb` for `len(a) + c` shapes; extend to `k * len(a) + c`).
2. The overflow check on `2 * i`: with i <= len(a) - 1 < 2^61 and k small, the product cannot overflow i64; use the `hi` bound when known (the alloc cap gives every length < 2^61, so `k * i` for literal k < 4 is safe; derive `hi` from `ub` facts via the 2^61 bound as range_limit already does for ranges).
3. A value read from a `[u8]` carries lo 0, hi 255 (u8_val does this); check why the write `out[j] = v` where v came from `@hex[...]` (a binary attribute read) still emits `defk_to_u8`: the attribute read path probably returns a plain i64 without the u8 facts; give it `u8_val`.

Verify with the fast-path check used in test/attributes_test.exs (grep the generated C) and measure the hex encoder before/after (examples/codecs.exs, encode alone was 1.5x; the decode side has the same shape).

Done when: the hex encoder's inner loop has no bounds check, no overflow check and no u8 range check in the generated C, with tests on the C for each, and the agreement properties still pass.

comments.text: Measured under load (other agents running on the machine): elixir examples/codecs.exs, 4 runs before (base 9c037bf compiler) and 4 after, each figure the script's best of 7, then the best of the 4 runs. 1 MB hex encode: defk encode16 0.601 -> 0.333 ms (1.8x faster); :binary.encode_hex 0.86-1.04 ms, so encode alone goes from ~1.5x to ~2.6x over the BIF. 1 MB hex decode (1 MB out): defk decode16 0.644 -> 0.503 ms (1.28x faster); :binary.decode_hex 1.61-1.89 ms, so ~2.6x -> ~3.2x. Round trip (the workload verdict): defk 1.243 -> 0.878 ms; speedup over the optimized baseline 1.99-2.02x in the quieter before runs (one read marginal) vs 2.66-2.89x after, verdict good in all after runs. Generated C of both loops now has no defk_put/defk_get, no defk_mul_i64/defk_add_i64, no defk_to_u8 (the attribute read already carried lo 0/hi 255 since defk-qx3; test added). The header numbers in examples/codecs.exs were not updated (taken under different conditions).

title: Range facts for constant multiples and alloc(2 * len): out[2 * i] keeps its bounds check
